head: """Skills registry — Agent Skills spec con extensiones locales.
Pattern: Agent Skills. Cada skill es una carpeta con SKILL.md.
Frontmatter YAML declara name + description + priority + requires.
Boot flow:
1. scan_skills() → list[SkillMeta]    (al boot del agente, ~10ms)
2. build_menu(skills) → str           (inyectado al system_prompt como
"# SKILLS AVAILABLE" + 1 linea
por skill: 50 tokens c/u)
3. build_critical_block(skills)       (skills con priority=critical se
eager-loaded full body)
4. load_skill_content(name) → str     (lazy: llamado por skill_load tool
cuando el LLM lo pide)
Diferencia vs microagents:
- microagent: contexto eager por trigger (knowledge en glossary, troubleshoot)
- skill: receta lazy on-demand. El LLM ve un MENU (name + description) y
decide SEMANTICAMENTE cual cargar via skill_load(). Sin keyword matching.
`priority` extension (no esta en el spec oficial):
- critical: eager-loaded full body en cada turn. Reservado para safety/
honestidad universales (e.g. purchase-guard).
- high/medium/low: solo aparecen en el menu (lazy). Cap por profile de
cuantas skill_load() puede emitir el LLM en un turn.
`requires` extension (eligibility filter):
- bins: lista de exes que deben estar en PATH (e.g. ["steam.exe"])
- any_bins: al menos uno debe estar en PATH (e.g. ["chrome", "edge"])
- env: lista de env vars que deben estar set (no vacias)
- os: lista de OS aceptados ("windows" | "linux" | "darwin")
Skills con requirements no cumplidos se ocultan del menu (LLM no las
selecciona).
Opt-out:
GEMMA4_SKILLS_OFF=1 desactiva todo el sistema (menu vacio, skill_load
retorna "skills disabled").
Limite por profile (cuantas skill_load() puede emitir el LLM en 1 turn):
standby:     0

GPU (~100ms, lo que el user ve en su panel). Fallback a WMI si psutil no está.
Devuelve un dict listo para _ok(**...) o un dict con 'error' para _err(**...). El

import subprocess
from typing import Any
def gpu_info_fast() -> Any:
"""GPU vía nvidia-smi (~100ms). Si no hay NVIDIA, marcador honesto (no spawnea

VRAM tengo?'). Best-effort."""
try:
proc = subprocess.run(
["nvidia-smi",
"--query-gpu=name,memory.total,memory.used,utilization.gpu,driver_version",
"--format=csv,noheader,nounits"],
capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=4)
gpus = []
for ln in (proc.stdout or "").strip().splitlines():
parts = [p.strip() for p in ln.split(",")]

head: """Per-tool logit head — the research's anti-bloat subset selector.
The four research reports' recommended architecture: a multi-label router head
emitting a per-tool logit with a PER-TOOL CALIBRATED THRESHOLD. The subset is
"tools whose logit clears their own bar" — not top-k, not a band. This is what
structurally prevents bloat: a flat-distribution query ("pausa") activates only
the tool(s) that individually clear threshold ({media}), not the whole cluster.
Runtime: one query embedding (already computed by semantic_router) · a 65×384
matmul · per-tool sigmoid · per-tool threshold compare. Sub-millisecond, numpy
only, no sklearn. Weights in versioned JSON (scripts/train_tool_head.py).
Returns the tools that fire, sorted by margin over their threshold (most
confident first), so the caller can keep the strongest and cap if needed.

import os
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any
_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "data" / "tool_head.json"  # reorg 2026-05-28
@dataclass
class ToolHead:
tools: list[str]
weights: Any           # np.ndarray [N, D]
biases: Any            # np.ndarray [N]
thresholds: Any        # np.ndarray [N]
def fire(self, embedding: Any) -> list[tuple[str, float]]:
"""Return (tool, margin) for every tool whose calibrated probability
clears its threshold, strongest margin first. margin = p - threshold."""
import numpy as np
v = np.asarray(embedding, dtype=np.float32)
z = self.weights @ v + self.biases
p = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-z))
